mainEntity.name: Can any interior partition wall be removed or relocated safely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Demolishing or altering an interior partition requires verifying whether the wall carries structural weight from roof trusses, ceiling joists, or upper stories. While non-load-bearing partitions can be safely removed or relocated once utilities are cleared, removing a load-bearing wall without temporary shoring and a properly sized header beam will compromise structural stability. A general contractor inspects joist direction, attic framing, and foundation support points to confirm whether a partition is structural or purely decorative before any framing is cut.
acceptedAnswer.description: Only non-load-bearing partitions can be removed freely; structural walls require temporary support posts and engineered header beams to maintain building stability.
